answer: Agents can bind voting weight to a unique human credential issued after an in-person check, then require a fresh, unlinkable proof of that credential for each contribution. The ledger accepts only one active credential per person, so minting thousands of agent accounts does not multiply influence. An attacker must recruit real people or defeat the check, paying for coordination and risking detection; the barrier is costly, not absolute. At dawn, the knoll’s local verifier can issue proofs without exposing names, while the horizon of trust remains limited to credentialed participants.
